output.brief: Owen: the fall in incidents is not real, so don't sign off the retainer cut or the bonus yet. Tessaline's audit trail shows 37 and 36 cases reached confirmed-incident status in Sep and Oct, which is in line with the roughly 38 a month before. Of those 73, 47 were later switched to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" by Brackwater's integration account. Each switch came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just as the SLA-warning flag was raised, and each had analyst confirmation notes. Those cases then dropped out of both the incident count and the containment-time and SLA figures. That is why containment looks like 100% and containment time looks faster. The vendor advisory for the connector version in use describes a bug that overwrites categories when an SLA warning fires, and the timing fits it. So this is probably a fault, though I haven't ruled out deliberate action. The API gateway log would show who made the changes. I'm fairly sure (about 80%) of the main conclusion. Next steps: put the 47 cases back as incidents, and have the in-house team and Halvard verify containment on each. Then remove the integration role's category-edit rights, fix or patch the connector, and hold the bonus. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Check whether any attacks went undetected, since the 28 dropped rules are not shown to be the cause.
